The lost seeds were rerun under a procedure that was fixed, and reviewed independently, before the rerun~\cite{JointTestRecovery2026}.
A determinism check fixed before the rerun (16 of 16 completed seeds rerun bitwise identically) shows that each recovered draw is the lost draw, so every submitted draw has been observed.
No recovered draw reaches the observed statistic in any test, claim variant or robustness variant, so no assignment of the lost draws changes any decision.

The recovered draws were evaluated in two ways: with the variant shifts of the primary evaluation held fixed (the \emph{fixed-shift} evaluation), and with the shifts recomputed on all draws (the \emph{recomputed-shift} evaluation).
The recovery's checks are narrower in scope than the main recomputation.
Only the fixed-shift evaluation was cross-checked independently.
The recomputed-shift evaluation was reproduced only by a standalone rerun of the same code, a consistency check rather than an independent recomputation.
The earlier stops rest on the calibration run's own re-application of the sequential rule and have no independent check.
The decisions of Table~\ref{tab:joint5d} remain those of the evaluation before recovery, at the $B$ at which its rule stopped.
